schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE DEPT (DEPTNO INT, NAME INT);
q1: SELECT DEPT.NAME AS DNAME, COUNT(*) AS C FROM DEPT AS DEPT GROUP BY DEPT.NAME HAVING DEPT.NAME = 10
q2: SELECT T2.DNAME, T2.CNT AS C FROM (SELECT DEPT0.NAME AS DNAME, COUNT(*) AS CNT FROM DEPT AS DEPT0 GROUP BY DEPT0.NAME) AS T2 WHERE T2.DNAME = 10
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DEPT.NAME AS DNAME, COUNT(*) AS C FROM DEPT AS DEPT GROUP BY DEPT.NAME HAVING DEPT.NAME = 10

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 is trying to count the number of departments with a specific name (10), which is not a valid operation since department names are of type INT and not strings. Q2, on the other hand, is trying to count the number of departments and then filter the result where the department name is 10, which is also not valid due to the same reason.
